items.prompt: Where did Dilnoza buy the lamp?
items.audio:
Dilnoza bought a blue desk lamp at a shop called Bright Home on Saturday morning. She paid twenty-four dollars for it. The lamp looked beautiful, and the seller, a young man named Marco, said it was the newest model. At home, Dilnoza put the lamp on her desk and pressed the button. Nothing happened. She tried another socket in the kitchen, but the lamp stayed dark. She felt sad because she needed it for her evening homework.

On Monday after school she took the lamp back to the shop with her receipt. A woman named Mrs. Clarke was standing behind the counter. Dilnoza says hello and explains that she bought the lamp two days ago, but it does not work. Mrs. Clarke looks at the lamp carefully and turns it upside down. She finds a small loose wire inside the base. She says she is very sorry and tells Dilnoza that she can choose a new lamp, or she can have her money back.

Dilnoza thinks for a moment. She likes the blue color, so she asks for the same model. Mrs. Clarke goes to the storeroom, but there are no blue lamps left. There is only a white one and a green one. Dilnoza picks the white one because it matches her desk. Mrs. Clarke tests it in front of her, and it works well. The light is bright and warm.

Before Dilnoza leaves, Mrs. Clarke gives her a small card. It says the lamp has a guarantee for one year. She also gives Dilnoza a free light bulb to say sorry for the problem. Dilnoza thanks her and walks home happily. That evening she finishes her homework under the new white light, and she tells her older brother that Bright Home is a good shop with kind people.

items.prompt: What is Rustam going to on Friday evening?
items.audio:
Rustam is going to his cousin's wedding on Friday evening. Last month he bought a dark gray suit, but the trousers are too long and the jacket is a little loose. On Tuesday afternoon he takes the suit to a small tailor shop near the bus station. The tailor is an old man named Mr. Petrov. He has gray hair and wears a measuring tape around his neck.

Rustam asks if the tailor can fix the suit before Friday. Mr. Petrov looks at the clothes and says the work is easy. He asks Rustam to put on the trousers and stand on a small wooden box. Then he puts little pins in the cloth. He says the trousers must be shorter by four centimeters. For the jacket, he wants to make the sides narrower, so it will fit Rustam better.

Rustam asks about the price. Mr. Petrov says the trousers cost eight dollars and the jacket costs twelve dollars, so the total is twenty dollars. He promises that everything will be ready on Thursday at five o'clock. He writes the date on a paper ticket and gives it to Rustam. Rustam must show the ticket when he comes back.

On Thursday, Rustam arrives a little early, but Mr. Petrov is already waiting with the suit in a clean plastic bag. Rustam tries it on behind a green curtain. The trousers are perfect now, and the jacket feels comfortable. He pays the money and thanks the tailor many times. Mr. Petrov smiles and tells him to enjoy the wedding. On Friday, Rustam wears the suit, and his cousin says he looks like a film star. Everybody at the party takes photos with him.

items.prompt: What does Aigerim study?
items.audio:
Aigerim is twenty years old, and she studies design at the university. Last week she got her first salary from a part-time job in a cafe. On Wednesday she goes to a bank on Green Street because she wants to open a savings account. She takes her passport and a student card with her, as her friend told her to do.

items.prompt: What color is Jasur's car?
items.audio:
Jasur has an old white car, and he loves it very much. After a long trip to the mountains, the car is covered with mud. On Sunday morning he drives to a car wash called Sparkle, which is next to a petrol station. There are three other cars in front of him, so he waits for fifteen minutes.

A worker named Oleg comes to his window and asks what kind of wash he would like. Jasur looks at the price board. A basic wash costs five dollars and only cleans the outside. A full wash costs ten dollars and also cleans the inside, the seats, and the floor. Jasur chooses the full wash because the inside of his car is dusty and full of old paper cups.

Oleg asks him to leave the keys and wait in the small cafe. Jasur orders a cup of black tea and sits near the window. He can see two workers washing his car with soap and water. They use a soft brush for the wheels and a cloth for the windows. Another worker cleans the seats with a vacuum cleaner.

After forty minutes, Oleg calls Jasur to the car. It looks like new. The windows are shining, and the inside smells like fresh lemons. Jasur pays ten dollars and adds two dollars as a tip because he is so pleased. Oleg gives him a card with a special offer. If Jasur comes again in two weeks, the wash will be half price.

Jasur thanks him and drives home slowly. He wants to keep the car clean as long as he can, so he decides to wash it every month.

items.prompt: What is the haircut for?
items.audio:
Malika wants to have a new haircut before her sister's graduation party. On Monday evening she calls a hair salon called Style House. A young man named Kamil answers the phone. He says hello and asks how he can help her.

Malika says she would like a haircut and a hair wash for this Saturday. Kamil checks the computer. He says the morning is full, but there are two free times in the afternoon. One is at one o'clock, and the other is at three thirty. Malika chooses three thirty because she has a class at the language center until noon and she wants time for lunch.

Kamil asks what she wants to do with her hair. Malika says it is long now, and she would like to cut about ten centimeters and keep the front part longer. He says the stylist called Zarina can do that very well. Then he asks for her name and her phone number. Malika spells her last name slowly, because Kamil writes it down wrong the first time.

He tells her the price. A haircut and a wash cost eighteen dollars. If she wants a special styling for the party, it costs another seven dollars. Malika decides to take the styling too. Kamil says she should come ten minutes early and bring a photo of the haircut she likes, because it helps the stylist.

Before the call ends, Kamil says the salon will send a message on Friday to remind her. If she cannot come, she must call at least one day before. Malika thanks him and says goodbye. She feels excited about the party and puts a reminder in her phone.

items.prompt: What did Bobur order?
items.audio:
Bobur ordered a pair of black running shoes from an online shop last Thursday. The website promised delivery in three days, but now it is already the following Wednesday, and the box has not arrived. He needs the shoes for a race in the city park on Sunday, so he is worried.

He calls the customer service number of the shop. A polite woman called Sandra answers. Bobur tells her his order number and explains the problem. Sandra checks the system and says she can see the parcel. It left the warehouse on Friday, but it got stuck in another city because of heavy snow on the roads. A truck with many parcels could not move for two days.

Sandra apologizes and says the parcel is now on a new truck. It will reach Bobur's city tomorrow morning, and a courier will bring it to his home by two o'clock in the afternoon. Bobur asks if she is sure. She says she cannot promise the exact minute, but the system shows a good chance. She also offers him a discount of ten percent for his next order, as a small way to say sorry.

Bobur is still a little unhappy, but he says thank you. He asks Sandra to send a message to his phone when the courier is near. She says she will do that and writes a note in the system.

The next day, at one thirty, the courier rings the bell. Bobur opens the door and takes the box. The shoes fit perfectly. On Sunday he runs seven kilometers in the park and finishes in the first twenty runners.

items.prompt: Until what time is the pharmacy open?
items.audio:
It is a cold Thursday evening, and Gulnora is not feeling well. She has a headache, a sore throat, and a cough that keeps her awake at night. She walks to a small pharmacy near her house, which is open until ten o'clock. Inside, a pharmacist named Mr. Karimov is arranging boxes on a shelf.

Gulnora says good evening and explains her problems. Mr. Karimov listens carefully and asks how long she has felt sick. She says it started three days ago. He asks if she has a fever. She says her temperature was thirty-seven point five this morning, which is only a little high. He nods and says it is probably a cold, not something serious.

He takes three things from the shelf. The first is a box of tablets for the headache, and she should take one after dinner, not more than three a day. The second is a bottle of sweet syrup for the cough. She should take two spoons before bed. The third is a packet of sweets for the sore throat. They have honey and lemon in them.

Mr. Karimov also gives her some advice. She must drink a lot of warm tea, stay at home, and sleep for at least eight hours. If she still has a fever after three more days, she should visit a doctor. Gulnora asks about the price, and he says the total is eleven dollars.

She pays, thanks him, and walks home slowly. At home she makes a cup of tea with honey, takes her medicine, and goes to bed early. After two days she feels much better.

items.prompt: Who goes to the shop with Sevara?
items.audio:
Sevara needs a new phone because her old one is slow and the battery is very weak. On Saturday she goes to an electronics shop with her older brother Timur, who knows a lot about technology. A salesman named Victor shows them two phones on the counter.

The first phone is called the Nova. It is blue, light, and costs two hundred and fifty dollars. It has a big screen and a good camera, which is important because Sevara loves taking photos of her cat. The battery lasts for about one day. The second phone is called the Orbit. It is black and a little heavier, and the price is three hundred and ten dollars. Its battery lasts for two days, and it has more memory, so she can keep many videos on it.

Timur holds both phones and thinks. He says the Orbit is stronger, but the Nova is easier to carry in a small bag. Sevara tries the cameras. She takes a picture of the shop window with each phone. The Nova gives brighter colors, but the Orbit makes sharper pictures at night.

Victor says the shop has a small sale this week. Anyone who buys the Orbit gets a free case and a screen cover. Sevara decides that this is a good reason to choose it. She also likes the long battery, because she travels to the university by bus for one hour every day.

She pays by card, and Victor puts the phone in a small box. On the way home, Timur says she made a clever choice. Sevara smiles and starts to move her photos to the new phone.

items.prompt: What happens to the laptop on Monday morning?
items.audio:
Farhod has a laptop that he uses for his work. On Monday morning, while he is writing an email, the screen suddenly turns black and the laptop makes a strange noise. He tries to switch it on again, but nothing happens. He is afraid because all his files are inside it.

After lunch, he carries the laptop to a repair shop called Fix It Fast, which is on the second floor of a market building. The owner, a tall man named Mr. Brown, welcomes him and puts the laptop on a table. He opens the back and looks inside with a small light. After a few minutes, he says the fan is full of dust and the hard disk is too hot. The laptop stopped to protect itself.

Farhod asks if his files are safe. Mr. Brown says yes, because the disk is not broken. He will clean the fan, put new paste on the processor, and copy the files to another disk to be safe. The work will take two days. The price is fifteen dollars, and he does not charge anything for copying the files.

Farhod agrees and fills in a small form with his name and phone number. Mr. Brown gives him a number, seventeen, and says that he will call when the laptop is ready.

On Wednesday at eleven in the morning, Farhod gets the call. He goes back to the shop and sees that the laptop looks clean and works quietly. Mr. Brown advises him to clean it every six months and never to put it on a soft bed or pillow. Farhod pays and promises to follow the advice.

items.prompt: What color is Nigora's coat?
items.audio:
Nigora has a beautiful cream coat that she bought last winter. Last Saturday at a family dinner, someone dropped a glass of red juice on the sleeve. She tried to clean it with water at home, but the stain became bigger. On Monday she takes the coat to a dry cleaner called White Cloud, which is near her office.

A kind woman named Mrs. Ivanova stands behind the counter. She takes the coat and looks at the sleeve under a strong light. She says that the stain is not too old, so it will probably come out. She asks Nigora if there is anything in the pockets. Nigora checks and finds a small pen and a bus ticket.

Mrs. Ivanova writes a paper tag with the number twenty-six and puts it on the coat. She says the cleaning takes three days. For a coat, the price is nine dollars. If Nigora wants the coat in one day, it costs five dollars more. Nigora does not need it so quickly, so she chooses the normal service.

Then Mrs. Ivanova gives her some advice. She says never to use hot water on a juice stain, because heat makes the color stay in the cloth. Cold water and a little salt are better. Nigora laughs and says she will remember it for next time.

On Thursday afternoon, she returns with the tag. The coat is in a long clear bag, and the stain is gone. It even smells fresh and clean. Nigora pays the money, thanks Mrs. Ivanova, and wears the coat home because the evening is cold and windy.

items.prompt: What are Dilshod and Zebo celebrating?
items.audio:
On Friday evening, Dilshod takes his wife Zebo to a restaurant called The Green Table to celebrate their fifth wedding anniversary. They have a table by the window, and a young waiter named Ben brings the menu. Dilshod orders grilled fish with rice, and Zebo chooses a mushroom soup and a salad.

The soup arrives quickly, and it is delicious. But after thirty minutes, the fish has still not come. Dilshod is hungry and a little angry. He calls the waiter and politely asks about his order. Ben looks surprised and goes to the kitchen to check. When he returns, he explains that the cook made a mistake and forgot the order.

Ben apologizes again and again. He says the fish will be ready in ten minutes, and the restaurant will give them a free dessert. However, when the fish finally arrives, it is cold, and there is no rice on the plate. Dilshod asks to speak with the manager.

The manager, a woman named Mrs. Petrova, comes to the table. She listens quietly and says she is very sorry for the bad evening. She takes the plate away and asks the kitchen to cook a new one. This time the fish is hot, fresh, and served with a big portion of rice. She also takes the cost of the main dish from the bill and offers them two cups of tea.

Dilshod and Zebo enjoy the dessert, which is a chocolate cake with a small candle. When they leave, Dilshod thanks the manager and says they will come back. He says a good restaurant is one that fixes its mistakes.

items.prompt: Where is Akmal flying?
items.audio:
Akmal has to go to the airport early on Sunday morning because his flight to Istanbul leaves at eight fifteen. He does not want to ask his friends for a lift, so on Saturday evening he calls a taxi company named City Wheels. A man called Pavel answers the phone.

Akmal says he needs a taxi for Sunday at five thirty in the morning. Pavel asks for the address. Akmal says he lives at number twelve, Navoi Street, in the third entrance of a gray building. Pavel writes it down and asks how many people are traveling. Akmal says he is alone, but he has two big suitcases. Pavel says that is no problem, because the car has a large trunk.

Then Akmal asks about the price. Pavel says the ride to the airport usually takes forty minutes, and the cost is fourteen dollars. A night or early morning ride has an extra charge of two dollars, so the total is sixteen dollars. Akmal can pay by cash or by card in the car.

Pavel says the driver will be a man called Anvar, who drives a silver car. He will send a message with the car number on Sunday at five o'clock, and he will call when he is outside the building. Akmal asks if the driver can wait if he is a few minutes late. Pavel says the driver waits for ten minutes for free.

Akmal thanks him and sets two alarms on his phone. On Sunday, the taxi is on time, and he arrives at the airport with plenty of time for coffee.

items.prompt: Where is the travel agency?
items.audio:
Laylo and her husband Sanjar want to spend their summer holiday by the sea. On Tuesday afternoon they visit a travel agency called Blue Sky, which is on the main square. A friendly agent named Olga invites them to sit down and offers them a glass of water.

Laylo says they would like to go for one week in July, and they do not want to spend more than nine hundred dollars together. Olga opens a big folder and shows two offers. The first is a hotel in Turkey, with breakfast and dinner, close to a quiet beach. It costs eight hundred and eighty dollars for two people. The second is a small apartment in Georgia, near the mountains and the sea, for seven hundred and fifty dollars, but meals are not included.

Sanjar likes the apartment because it is cheaper, and he wants to cook fresh fish. Laylo prefers the hotel, because she does not want to cook on holiday. Olga explains that the flight to Turkey is shorter, only three hours, while the trip to Georgia is five hours with one change.

After a few minutes, they choose Turkey. Olga says they must pay a deposit of two hundred dollars today and the rest one month before the trip. She also reminds them to check their passports, because a passport must be valid for at least six months.

Laylo and Sanjar sign the contract and pay the deposit. Olga gives them a small bag with a map and a guide book. On the way home, they are both very excited and start to plan the days at the beach.

items.prompt: Why do Zarina and Eldor need furniture?
items.answer: they have moved into a new flat
items.audio:
Zarina and her husband Eldor have just moved into a new flat, and they need furniture. On Saturday morning they go to a big furniture shop called Home Comfort, which is on the edge of the city. First they look for a sofa. A salesman named Mr. Hakim shows them several choices in the living room section.

They like a gray sofa with soft cushions. It is two meters long, and it costs four hundred and twenty dollars. Mr. Hakim says it is a very popular model, and it is made from strong cloth that is easy to clean. Eldor sits on it and says it is very comfortable, but Zarina worries that it is too large for their small room. She measures the wall with a tape and decides that it will fit.

Next they need a dining table for four people. They find a wooden table with four chairs for three hundred dollars. The wood is light brown, and the legs are strong. Mr. Hakim says that if they buy both the sofa and the table, the shop will take fifty dollars off the price.

They also ask about delivery. Mr. Hakim says that delivery is free for orders over five hundred dollars, and the truck can come on Tuesday or Wednesday. The workers will carry everything upstairs and put the table together. Zarina chooses Wednesday, because she will be at home in the afternoon.

They pay for the furniture and take a receipt. Mr. Hakim shakes their hands and wishes them a happy new home. On the way out, Zarina buys a small green plant for the window.
options: they have moved into a new flat

items.prompt: When will the wedding be?
items.answer: On the second Saturday of May
items.audio:
Dilnoza is sitting in her aunt's kitchen with a big notebook. She is going to marry Aziz on the second Saturday of May, and she wants to check the plan with her aunt Malika. First, they talk about the place. Dilnoza says the wedding will be in a green garden near Samarkand, because the family hall is too small for two hundred guests. The garden has tall trees and a little river, and Aziz thinks it is the most beautiful place in the city.

Then Malika asks about the food. Dilnoza says her mother will cook plov in four huge pots, and a bakery in the old town will make the bread and the cake. The cake will have three levels and white flowers made of sugar. Malika smiles and says she will bring fruit and sweets from her own shop. She also asks about music. Dilnoza answers that a young singer called Farhod will sing from six o'clock, and a small band will play after dinner. Her little cousins want to dance, so there will be a big space in front of the tables.

At the end, they talk about the guests and the day itself. The first guests will come at four o'clock, and the ceremony will start at half past four. Dilnoza worries about the weather, so Aziz's brother will rent two large white tents. Malika tells her not to worry too much. She says the most important thing is to be happy. Dilnoza writes one last sentence in her notebook: call the photographer on Monday. Then she closes it and drinks her tea. She feels excited, but she also feels ready, because every small detail now has a name, a time and a person who will help her.
options: On the second Saturday of May
On the first Sunday of June
On the last Friday of April

items.prompt: Which instrument does Jasur play?
items.audio:
On Thursday afternoon, the school orchestra has its last rehearsal before the spring concert. Jasur is fifteen and plays the violin. He arrives at the music hall at three o'clock, and his teacher, Mrs. Karimova, is already there. She is putting chairs in a big half circle. There are twenty-two students in the orchestra, and the concert is on Saturday evening at seven o'clock. Everyone is a little nervous.

The rehearsal begins with a slow song, and it goes well. Then the orchestra plays a fast folk tune. The drums start too early, and Mrs. Karimova stops the music. She asks everyone to listen to each other. They play it again three times. The last time it sounds perfect, and the students clap. After a short break with water and apples, Jasur plays a solo. He has practised it every evening for a month. His hands are cold, but he plays all the notes and does not stop once.

At half past five, Mrs. Karimova gives them some advice. She tells them to eat a light dinner on Saturday and to arrive one hour early. Everyone must wear a white shirt and black trousers. A girl called Gulnora asks if parents can take photos. The teacher says yes, but only after the concert, because flashes disturb the players. Before going home, Jasur helps to carry the music stands to the back room. His mother is waiting outside with a warm coat. She asks how it went. Jasur says it was tiring but good, and he promises to practise one more time on Friday morning.

items.prompt: When was the neighbours' meeting?
items.audio:
Every year, the people in Madina's building organise a New Year party in the courtyard. This year the meeting was on the fifteenth of December, and eleven neighbours came to Madina's flat. Old Mr. Rustam, who has lived there for thirty years, said the party must start at nine in the evening and end after midnight. Everyone agreed. They also decided that each family would pay ten dollars, and the money would buy lights, juice and a small gift for every child.

Next, the neighbours shared the work. Madina's father will put a big fir tree in the middle of the courtyard. A young couple, Sardor and Lola, will decorate it with silver balls and colourful lights. Mrs. Zebo is famous for her salads, so she will make a huge bowl of olivier. Two teenagers, Timur and Bobur, will take care of the music. They have a speaker and a long list of songs, from old Uzbek tunes to modern pop.

The best part of the plan is a surprise. A neighbour who works in a theatre will come dressed as Grandfather Frost and give presents to the children at eleven thirty. At midnight, everybody will go outside and count the last ten seconds together. Then there will be a small fireworks show, but only ten minutes long, because the building has many babies and pets. Madina is happy with the plan. She will write the list on a large sheet of paper and put it on the door of the building, so that nobody forgets their task. Her little brother already asks every morning how many days are left.

items.prompt: Why is the party at Nigora's grandmother's house?
items.audio:
Shahlo will be eighteen on Sunday, and her best friend Nigora is planning a surprise party. They are going to do it at Nigora's grandmother's house, because it has a big garden. Nigora has told only five people about the plan, and she has asked all of them to keep it secret. Her cousin Anvar has the hardest job. On Sunday, at two o'clock, he must take Shahlo to the new shopping centre and keep her there for two hours.

While they are away, the other friends will work fast. Nigora and her mother will bake a chocolate cake with eighteen candles. Two boys, Ilhom and Sherzod, will hang balloons and a long yellow sign that says Happy Birthday. Shahlo loves yellow flowers, so the guests will bring sunflowers instead of roses. There will be pizza, lemonade and Shahlo's favourite dessert, which is apple pie. The music will be quiet at first, because everybody has to hide in the living room.

There is one problem. Shahlo is very clever and often guesses secrets. Last week she asked Nigora why she was so busy. Nigora said she had a lot of homework. To be safe, she also wrote a false message on the group chat, saying the party would be next month. At four o'clock, Anvar will send a short text, and Nigora will switch off the lights. When Shahlo opens the door, everybody will shout surprise. Nigora hopes Shahlo will laugh, not cry. Her gift is a small silver necklace with a letter S, and she has already hidden it in her school bag.
options: It is near the shopping centre

items.prompt: When does Akmal finish university?
items.audio:
Akmal finishes university in June, and his family is planning a graduation dinner for him. His mother, Feruza, made the first list at the weekend. She wants a quiet restaurant near the river, with a room for thirty people. Her sister has found one called Silk Road, which has a long table and a balcony. The owner is a friendly man named Mr. Haydar, and he gave them a good price if they come on a Tuesday evening.

The family talked about the menu for almost an hour. Akmal's grandfather asked for traditional soup and grilled lamb. His little sister Sevara wanted ice cream, but his father said fruit would be healthier. In the end they chose three dishes, a salad, lamb with rice, and a big cake with a book on top. The cake is a joke, because Akmal has read more than a hundred books during his studies. He studied engineering and was the best student in his group.

Then they talked about speeches. His father will say a few words first, and then his old teacher, Mrs. Yusupova, will tell a short story about Akmal's first day at university. Akmal will thank everybody at the end. He is afraid of speaking in front of many people, so he is already writing notes. After dinner, the family wants to take a group photo on the bridge, because the lights there are pretty at night. Feruza is also saving some money for a present. She plans to give Akmal a leather bag for his first job. He has an interview next month at a car factory, and he wants to look professional.

items.prompt: What time does the final start?
items.audio:
Tomorrow is the biggest day of the year for Bekzod and his school football team. They are playing the city final against School Number Twelve at the central stadium at four o'clock. The coach, Mr. Anvarov, called a meeting after training today. He said the boys must sleep early, drink a lot of water and eat pasta for lunch. The bus will leave the school at one thirty, and nobody can be late.

Mr. Anvarov also explained the plan for the game. The other team is fast, but its goalkeeper is small. So Bekzod, who plays in the middle, will pass quickly to Doston, the tall player on the right. Doston has scored nine goals this season. The defenders must stay close to the other team's best player, a boy with a red number seven shirt. Mr. Anvarov also changed one thing. The captain, Javlon, has a sore knee, so he will start on the bench and come on in the second half.

After the meeting, the team went to the cafe next to school. They talked about the supporters. About two hundred students and teachers are going to come, and the girls' choir will sing before the game. Bekzod's father is making a big blue flag because blue is the colour of the team. Bekzod is nervous, but he is also very proud. He has played football since he was six. Before bed, he wants to clean his boots and pack his bag with a clean shirt, two socks and a bottle of water. If they win, the school will give each player a small gold medal.

items.prompt: How long does the festival last?
items.audio:
Good morning, listeners. This is your city news, and today we have all the details about the Spring Flower Festival in Namangan. The festival begins on Friday, the twentieth of April, and lasts for three days. It will take place in Central Park, which is near the old bazaar. The opening ceremony is at ten o'clock, and the mayor will cut a long green ribbon. The entrance is free for children under twelve. Adults pay two dollars.

There is something for everybody. On Friday, there is a big flower parade with twenty cars and many dancers in colourful dresses. On Saturday, the park will have a market with local crafts, honey, tea and sweets. The most popular event is the painting competition for children, which starts at eleven. The winner will get a set of professional paints. On Sunday evening, there will be a concert by the famous singer Munisa Rizayeva, and the festival will finish with fireworks at nine o'clock.

Organisers have also asked people to follow a few rules. Please do not drive to the park, because there is not enough parking. Buses number five and eleven will go there every ten minutes, and they are free during the festival. Please bring your own water bottle, because the organisers want less plastic. If you lose something, go to the small information tent near the main gate. More than four hundred volunteers will help visitors. Many of them are students from the local university. We hope the weather will be sunny. Enjoy the festival, and thank you for listening to your city news.

items.prompt: Why does the hospital need money?
items.audio:
Last month, Laylo decided to organise a charity run in her small town. She works as a nurse in the children's hospital, and the hospital needs money for new beds. She asked her friend Otabek, who is a sports teacher, to help her. Together they chose a route along the lake and agreed that the run would be five kilometres long. The date was the first Sunday of October, and the start was at eight in the morning.

At first, Laylo was afraid that nobody would come. She made posters and put them in shops, schools and the bus station. She also made a short video, and her cousin shared it with his friends. Soon, more than three hundred people wrote their names on the list. Each runner paid six dollars and got a green T-shirt and a bottle of water. A local bakery gave free bread rolls for all the runners, and a pharmacy sent two first-aid workers.

On the day of the race, the weather was cool and clear. Grandmothers, children and even a man with a small dog joined the run. The fastest runner was a student named Sanjar, who finished in twenty minutes. Otabek stood at the finish line with a megaphone and cheered for everyone. Laylo walked the whole way with her mother, who was seventy years old and very proud. In the end, the run collected almost two thousand dollars. The hospital director cried a little when he heard the news. Laylo is already planning another run next spring, and this time she wants to add a short race for children under ten.

items.prompt: What will Kamila study in Toronto?
items.audio:
Our friend Kamila is moving to Canada in two weeks, so her classmates are planning a farewell party. Kamila has lived in Andijan all her life, and she is going to study computer science in Toronto. Her best friends, Dildora and Eldor, are the organisers. They want the party to be special but not sad. They are going to hold it on Saturday afternoon in the school yard, because Kamila loves the old apple tree there.

The plan has three parts. First, everybody will sit under the tree and eat lunch. Dildora's father will cook shashlik, and the girls will bring salads and cakes. Second, each friend will give Kamila a small letter. Eldor has asked the class to write one nice memory, and he will put all the letters in a blue box. Kamila can open the box on the plane. Third, there will be a game. The class has made a quiz with twenty questions about Kamila's life. The winner will get a small prize, which is a keyring in the shape of a mountain.

The friends have also ordered something unusual. A photographer will take a photo of the whole class, and Dildora will make a big book with the best pictures. She is going to give it to Kamila as the main present. The party will end at six o'clock, when Kamila's parents come to take her home. Dildora feels sad when she thinks about the day. But Eldor reminds her that Kamila will call every Sunday, and the class can visit her in the summer. Nobody knows yet if that is possible, but it is a nice idea.

items.prompt: Whose turn was it to choose the film this week?
items.audio:
Every Friday, the Nazarov family has a movie night, and this week it was Sevinch's turn to choose the film. She is twelve years old and loves animal stories. Her older brother Jamshid wanted a science fiction film, but Sevinch won because she had waited for three weeks. Her choice was a story about a lost dog that walks across a whole country to find his family. Her father said the film was nearly two hours long, so they needed to start early, at seven o'clock.

Preparing for the movie is a big part of the fun. Her mother made popcorn in a large pot and added a little salt and butter. Jamshid carried the blankets and pillows into the living room and made a soft place on the floor. Their grandmother does not like loud films, so she brought her own tea and sat in the big chair. The cat, Mushuk, always comes too, and she usually sleeps on Sevinch's knees.

Before the film, the family has one rule. Everybody must turn off their phones, and nobody can talk during the story. After the movie, each person says one thing they liked. This time, Sevinch said the dog's friendship with a small bird was her favourite part. Jamshid, who did not want the film, admitted that the ending made him cry a little. Their father laughed and said he cried too. Next Friday, it will be their father's turn. He wants to show an old comedy from his childhood, and the children are already guessing which one it will be.

items.prompt: How many people took part in the contest?
items.audio:
Last Saturday, the community centre held a cooking contest for amateur cooks. Twelve people took part, and the theme was a dinner for four people with a budget of fifteen dollars. The judges were a chef called Mr. Abdulla, a food blogger named Zarina and a local grandmother who is famous for her pies. The contest began at ten in the morning and each cook had ninety minutes to prepare one main dish and one dessert.

Our reporter watched the best cooks. A young man named Davron made chicken with rice and dried fruit. He said the recipe was from his uncle, and he used only one pot to save money. A woman called Mohira cooked fish with lemon and potatoes. She had a problem, because her oven was too hot, and the first potatoes became black. She started again and finished with only four minutes left. The crowd clapped loudly for her.

The winner was a teenager named Ulugbek, who is just sixteen. He prepared a vegetable soup with fresh herbs and a warm apple dessert with cinnamon. The judges said his food was simple, but the taste was balanced and the plates looked beautiful. His prize was a new set of kitchen knives and a free cooking course for three months. Ulugbek said he learned to cook from watching his father, who works in a bakery. The second place went to Davron. The community centre is planning another contest in the winter, and it will be for children only. Anyone who wants to join can leave a name at the front desk. The centre also asks for volunteers to help wash dishes.

items.prompt: How many days will the fair last?

The Spring Book Fair will open at our town library next Wednesday, and the librarian, Mrs. Gulchehra, has given us the plan. The fair will last five days, from Wednesday to Sunday, and it will take place in the big hall on the second floor. It opens at nine in the morning and closes at six in the evening. More than forty publishers and small bookshops are coming from different cities, and many books will be cheaper than usual.

Every day has a special event. On Wednesday, a famous children's writer called Shirin Aliyeva will read a story for young visitors at eleven o'clock. On Thursday, there will be a talk about how to choose a good book, and a poet will sign copies of his new collection. Friday is the day for students, who can buy any book with a thirty percent discount if they show their school card. At the weekend, there will be a used book corner, where people can exchange old books for new ones. Nothing in that corner costs more than one dollar.

Mrs. Gulchehra also described the new reading room. It has twelve armchairs, a quiet lamp for every table and a small cafe that sells tea and biscuits. She said that the library wants to give free books to the village school in the mountains. Visitors can leave a children's book in a special red box near the entrance, and volunteers will send the books at the end of the month. Last year, people gave almost three hundred books. This year, the librarian hopes for five hundred. She says that reading together makes a town stronger, and she invites every family to come.

items.prompt: Where will the reunion take place?
items.audio:
Every summer, the Yusupov family has a big reunion, and this year it will take place in a village near Fergana at the house of Grandfather Karim. He is eighty years old and has six children, fourteen grandchildren and three great-grandchildren. Some relatives live far away, so the reunion is the only time when everyone meets. This year, forty-five people have promised to come. Aunt Nodira, who lives in Moscow, will arrive by plane on Thursday, and the others will come by car or bus on Friday.

The women of the family have prepared the plan. On Friday evening, everyone will have a welcome dinner in the garden, with long tables under the grape trees. On Saturday morning, the children will play games and the men will repair the old fence. In the afternoon, the family will plant a small walnut tree to remember the day. Each child will put a handful of earth around it. Grandfather says the tree will grow with the family, and in twenty years it will give a lot of nuts.

The best part is a photo session on Saturday at five o'clock. They have asked a professional photographer, a cousin named Rano, to take a large group picture. They will hang the picture in the hall of the house, next to older photos from the past. After the photo, the family will sing together and listen to Grandfather's stories about his youth. The evening will end with watermelon, because it is his favourite fruit. On Sunday, everybody will help to clean the house and then travel home. Nodira says she is bringing a suitcase full of presents, and nobody is allowed to look inside.

items.prompt: Where do the friends want to go?
items.audio:
Four friends, Behzod, Ozoda, Shaxzod and Kamron, are planning a weekend camping trip to the Chimgan mountains. They talked about it on the phone for an hour yesterday. They want to leave on Friday after school and come back on Sunday afternoon. Kamron's older brother has a small van, and he agreed to drive them there for twenty dollars. The trip takes about two hours, and they hope to arrive before dark, at around six o'clock.

Ozoda is the most careful of the group, so she made a list of the things to bring. They need two tents, four sleeping bags and a gas stove. Behzod will bring a map, a torch and a first-aid kit, because his mother is a doctor and she showed him how to use it. Shaxzod is responsible for food. He will buy bread, eggs, rice, tea and some tinned fish. They also want to take a guitar, because Kamron plays it very well, and they can sing around the fire. They decided not to bring speakers, since they want to hear the river.

The friends also made a few rules. Nobody can walk alone far from the camp. They will take all their rubbish back to the city. If it rains, they will stay in the tents and play cards. On Saturday morning, they plan to walk up to a small waterfall, which takes three hours. Ozoda says that the water there is very cold, but the view is wonderful. Behzod is worried about mosquitoes, so he is going to buy a special spray. They all agreed to meet at the bus station at three thirty on Friday. Kamron is already so excited that he cannot sleep.

items.prompt: When is Navruz celebrated?
items.audio:
Navruz is the spring festival of the new year, and it is celebrated on the twenty-first of March. In the village of Gijduvon, the Rakhimov family has prepared for it for two weeks. Grandmother Halima always says that a clean house brings luck, so the whole family cleaned every room, washed the windows and painted the gate green. Her granddaughter Zarnigor, who is ten, helped to hang bright scarves in the yard.

The most important food for Navruz is sumalak, a sweet dish made from wheat. It cooks all night in a huge pot, and the women sing songs while they take turns to stir it. Zarnigor stayed awake until midnight this year, which was her first time. Grandmother puts a few clean stones in the bottom of the pot, so that the sumalak does not burn. In the morning, the family tastes it first, and then they share it with all the neighbours. The family also prepares a table with seven dishes, and each of them has a special meaning.

On the festival day, the whole village goes to the main square. There are horse games, wrestling and a big stage where children sing and dance. Zarnigor will recite a short poem about spring at eleven o'clock. Her father will play the doira, a traditional drum, in the village band. In the afternoon, the family visits their relatives and brings small gifts, such as sweets and dried fruit. Grandmother says that on Navruz you must forgive old arguments and start the year with a kind heart. At sunset, the young people light a small fire and jump over it three times. Everybody wishes each other good health, peace and a rich harvest.

The most important food for Navruz is sumalak, a sweet dish made from wheat. It cooks all night in a huge pot, and the women sing songs while they take turns to stir it. Zarnigor stayed awake until midnight this year, which was her first time. Grandmother puts a few clean stones in the bottom of the pot, so that the sumalak does not burn. In the morning, the family tastes it first, and then they share it with all the neighbours. The family also prepares a table with seven dishes, and each of them has a special meaning.

On the festival day, the whole village goes to the main square. There are horse games, wrestling and a big stage where children sing and dance. Zarnigor will recite a short poem about spring at eleven o'clock. Her father will play the doira, a traditional drum, in the village band. In the afternoon, the family visits their relatives and brings small gifts, such as sweets and dried fruit. Grandmother says that on Navruz you must forgive old arguments and start the year with a kind heart. At sunset, the young people light a small fire and jump over it three times. Everybody wishes each other good health, peace and a rich harvest.

items.prompt: What caused the closure?
items.audio:
Attention, please. This is a message from the Tashkent Metro. Because of a water pipe problem, the Chilonzor line will be closed this weekend. The closure begins on Saturday at six in the morning and ends on Monday at five in the morning. Between Beruniy station and Olmazor station, no trains will run at all. Trains will still run on the other lines as usual.

To help passengers, the city will provide free buses. The buses will leave every eight minutes from outside each closed station. The yellow buses have the letter M on the front. Please follow the orange signs in the station to find the bus stop. The buses are free, so you do not need to buy a ticket, but you must still tap your travel card at the door. The journey by bus takes about thirty minutes, which is ten minutes longer than the train.

Workers will replace two old pipes and clean the tunnel. The manager of the metro, Mrs Gulnora Saidova, says that she is sorry for the problem. She says the repair is necessary because last month water came into the tunnel after the heavy rain, and one train stopped for an hour.

If you are going to the football stadium on Sunday evening, please leave home earlier, because the buses will be very busy. Passengers who use wheelchairs can ask a station worker for a special bus, which is free and comes every twenty minutes. You can also find more information on the metro website or by calling the number on the posters. Thank you for your patience, and have a safe weekend.

Good evening, parents and students of Green Hill School. This is Mr Anvar Yusupov, the head teacher. I am calling with important news. Because of the heavy snow tonight, the school will be closed tomorrow, Thursday. About thirty centimetres of snow fell today, and the weather office says that another twenty centimetres will arrive before morning. The roads near the school are icy, and the school buses cannot drive safely.

Students should stay at home tomorrow. Please do not wait at the bus stop. Teachers will put homework on the school website by eight in the morning. Younger students in grades one to four will have a reading task and a short drawing task. Older students will have a maths worksheet and a science video to watch. items.prompt: What does the new bridge connect?
items.answer: The old town and the new hospital
items.audio:
Good afternoon. This is the lunchtime news with Malika Nazarova. Our main story today is about the Red Bridge, which opened this morning after two years of work. The bridge crosses the river Zarafshan, and it connects the old town with the new hospital. The mayor, Mr Jasur Tursunov, cut a red ribbon at ten o'clock, and about five hundred people came to watch.

The old bridge was built in nineteen sixty and was very narrow. Many drivers waited for half an hour each morning to cross it. The new bridge has four lanes for cars, a lane for bicycles, and a wide path for people who walk. It is two hundred metres long, and it cost eight million dollars. The money came from the city and from a national fund.

Many people are very happy. A taxi driver named Sherzod says his journey to the hospital now takes five minutes instead of twenty. A student named Aisha says she likes the bicycle lane because it is safe and has lights at night.

However, not everyone is pleased. Some shop owners near the old road say they will have fewer customers, because fewer cars will pass their shops. The mayor says the town will build a new market near the bridge next year.

The bridge is open every day from six in the morning until midnight. Heavy lorries are not allowed on it, and they must use the ring road. Police will check the traffic carefully this week. That is all for the main news. After the break, we will bring you the sport and the weather.
options: The old town and the new hospital

Good morning, drivers. This is the Radio City traffic report with Farhod Ismoilov. It is seven thirty on a cold, wet Monday morning, and the roads are very busy. Let me start with the worst news. There was an accident on Navoi Avenue near the central market. A bus and a small white van hit each other at about six forty. Nobody is badly hurt, but one lane is closed, and traffic is moving very slowly. The police say the road will be clear by nine o'clock. Please use Amir Temur Street instead.

On the ring road, the news is better. Traffic is moving well in both directions, though there is a short delay near the airport turn, because workers are painting new white lines on the road. Please drive slowly there.

Now some news about the buses. Buses number five and number twelve are running about fifteen minutes late today because of the rain. Bus number twenty is running as normal. If you take the train, there are no problems at all, and all trains are on time.

Parking is difficult near the hospital, because a large truck is blocking the entrance to the car park. If you are visiting a patient, we suggest you take a taxi or walk from the park.

A short weather note. The rain will stop at ten o'clock, but the roads will stay slippery, so please keep a safe distance from the car in front. Our next traffic report is in twenty minutes. Until then, drive carefully, and enjoy the music with Radio City.

items.prompt: What was the building before it was a museum?
items.audio:
Welcome to the news from the city of Bukhara. Today the new Silk Road Museum opens its doors to visitors. The museum is in a beautiful old building near the main square. Before this, the building was a school for more than eighty years, and then it was empty for ten years. The city spent three years changing it into a museum.

Inside, there are five large rooms. The first room tells the story of the old trade roads, with maps and small models of camels. The second room shows silk, carpets, and beautiful clothes. In the third room, children can touch some of the objects and try on traditional hats. The fourth room has old coins and jewellery, and the last room has a small cinema, which shows a short film every hour.

The director, Mrs Nigora Rahimova, says she wants every family to visit. For this reason, the museum is free on the first Sunday of each month. On other days, a ticket for an adult costs fifty thousand soums, and a ticket for a student costs twenty thousand. Children under seven do not pay.

The museum is open from nine in the morning until six in the evening, from Tuesday to Sunday. It is closed on Mondays. There is a gift shop on the ground floor, which sells postcards, scarves, and books. On the roof, there is a cafe with a lovely view of the town, and it serves tea and sweet pastries.

Guided tours in English start at eleven o'clock and at three o'clock. You do not need to book a place. Just come to the front desk a few minutes before the tour begins.

items.prompt: Which fruit is half price?

Attention, shoppers. Welcome to Fresh Market on Mustaqillik Street. We have some wonderful offers for you this week, starting today and ending on Sunday night. Please listen carefully.

In the fruit and vegetable section, apples are half price. A kilo of red apples costs only six thousand soums. Fresh tomatoes are also cheap this week, and if you buy two kilos, you get the third kilo free. Our bananas come from Ecuador, and they are on sale at the front of the shop.

In the bakery, you can buy two loaves of bread and get one sweet bun for free. The bakery makes fresh bread at seven in the morning and again at four in the afternoon. Please come then if you like warm bread.

At the dairy counter, all yoghurts have a ten percent discount. Milk costs the same as last week, but there is a special offer for large boxes of eggs. A box of thirty eggs costs twenty thousand soums.

We also have a new offer for our customers with a Fresh Market card. If you spend one hundred thousand soums or more, you will receive a free reusable bag, which is made from recycled plastic. You can ask for a card at the customer desk near the entrance. It is free, and it takes only two minutes.

For families, there is a play area for children next to the pharmacy, and a student called Kamila will look after the children while you shop. It is open from ten o'clock to six o'clock.

Finally, the shop will stay open until eleven o'clock every evening this week. Thank you for shopping with us.

In the fruit and vegetable section, apples are half price. A kilo of red apples costs only six thousand soums. Fresh tomatoes are also cheap this week, and if you buy two kilos, you get the third kilo free. Our bananas come from Ecuador, and they are on sale at the front of the shop.

In the bakery, you can buy two loaves of bread and get one sweet bun for free. The bakery makes fresh bread at seven in the morning and again at four in the afternoon. Please come then if you like warm bread.

We also have a new offer for our customers with a Fresh Market card. If you spend one hundred thousand soums or more, you will receive a free reusable bag, which is made from recycled plastic. You can ask for a card at the customer desk near the entrance. It is free, and it takes only two minutes.

For families, there is a play area for children next to the pharmacy, and a student called Kamila will look after the children while you shop. It is open from ten o'clock to six o'clock.

Finally, the shop will stay open until eleven o'clock every evening this week. Thank you for shopping with us.

items.prompt: Who announced the strike?
items.audio:
Here is an important travel notice from National Railways. The train drivers' union has announced a strike for next Wednesday and Thursday. This means that many trains will not run on those two days. We are very sorry for the problem, and we want to help you plan your journey.

On Wednesday, only one train in three will run. The fast train between Tashkent and Samarkand will leave at seven in the morning and at five in the afternoon only. On Thursday, the situation will be a little better, and about half of the trains will run. There will be no night trains on either day.

If you have a ticket for a train that is cancelled, you can have your money back, or you can change your ticket for another day. You can do this on our website, at the station, or by phone. The refund will come to your bank card in about five working days. Please do not come to the station if your train is cancelled, because the ticket office will be very crowded.

The drivers say they want better pay and shorter working days. They say they now work ten hours a day, and they want to work eight. The railway company says it is ready to talk, and a meeting will take place on Monday at two o'clock.

If the meeting goes well, the strike may stop. We will put the latest news on our website on Monday evening and send a text message to all passengers.

In the meantime, you can travel by bus. Extra buses will leave from the main station every hour. Thank you for understanding.

items.prompt: When does the warning start?
items.audio:
This is a weather warning from the national weather service. A strong storm is coming to the north of the country tonight. The warning starts at six o'clock this evening and lasts until noon tomorrow. People in the towns of Nukus, Muynak, and Kungrad should listen carefully.

The storm will bring very strong wind. In some places, the wind will reach ninety kilometres an hour. It will also bring heavy rain, and in the hills, the rain may become snow after midnight. Temperatures will fall from fifteen degrees to just two degrees by morning.

What should you do? First, stay at home if you can. Do not drive at night, because trees may fall across the roads. Second, put your garden chairs, flower pots, and bicycles inside, because the wind can blow them away. Third, charge your phone and keep a torch near your bed, because there may be power cuts. Please do not use candles, because they can cause fires.

If you live near the river, please watch the water carefully. The river Amu Darya may rise by one metre. The local council has opened a safe shelter in the sports hall of School number seven. Anyone who needs to leave home can go there. It has beds, food, and hot drinks, and it is free.

Farmers should keep animals in a barn tonight. Fishermen should not go out on the lake.

The weather will improve tomorrow afternoon. By Friday, we expect sunshine and light winds. We will give another report at ten o'clock tonight, and our website has a live map. Please stay safe.

Welcome to the evening sports news. Last night, in the big city derby, Bunyodkor beat Pakhtakor by three goals to two. More than twenty thousand fans came to the stadium, and the weather was warm and dry.

Pakhtakor scored first, after only six minutes. Their striker, Eldor, kicked the ball from outside the box, and the goalkeeper could not stop it. Bunyodkor answered quickly. In the twenty-second minute, a young player named Sardor, who is only eighteen, scored with his head. Just before half time, Bunyodkor scored again, and at the break it was two to one.

In the second half, Pakhtakor scored again in the sixtieth minute, and the game was two all. Everyone thought it would be a draw. But in the last minute, a long pass found Sardor, and he scored his second goal. The crowd went wild. The coach, Mr Alisher Normatov, said it was the best night of his life. He said his team worked very hard in training this week.

In other sports news, the national swimming team returned from Dubai with four medals. They won one gold, two silver, and one bronze. The gold medal went to Nilufar, aged sixteen, in the one hundred metre race.

Finally, tickets for next Saturday's tennis final are now on sale. The final will be at the city tennis centre at four in the afternoon. Tickets cost thirty thousand soums and can be bought online.

That is all for sport. Join us again tomorrow.

items.prompt: How many runners will take part?
items.audio:
Attention, residents of Tashkent. This is a message from the city council about the Spring Marathon, which takes place this Sunday. More than eight thousand runners will take part, so many roads in the centre will be closed.

The race starts at eight o'clock in the morning in front of the Opera Theatre and finishes in Independence Square. The roads on the route will close at six in the morning and open again at two in the afternoon. Closed roads include Amir Temur Avenue, Shota Rustaveli Street, and the road beside the river. Please do not park on these streets from Saturday night, because police will move any cars left there.

Buses will not use the centre during the race. Bus lines three and nine will start and end at the Chorsu bazaar, and line fourteen will use the ring road. The metro will run as normal, and it will open an hour earlier, at five in the morning, so runners and families can arrive in time. Taxis will not be able to enter the area, and the best way to reach the race is on foot or by metro.

If you live on the route and need to leave home by car, please call the number on your letter. Doctors and ambulances will be able to cross the route at special points.

Runners can choose a full race of forty-two kilometres, a half race of twenty-one kilometres, or a family run of five kilometres. The family run begins at ten o'clock. Money from the race will help build a new playground at the children's hospital.

Come and cheer for the runners. There will be music, free water, and fruit on the route. Thank you for your help.

items.prompt: What was on the land before the park?
items.audio:
Good news for the people of Namangan. After eighteen months of work, the new Friendship Park will open next Saturday at ten o'clock. It is the biggest park in the city, and it is built on the land of an old factory. The factory closed twenty years ago, and for a long time the land was empty and dirty.

The park has a big green lawn, a lake, and more than two thousand new trees. Workers planted apple, cherry, and plane trees. Around the lake there is a path for walking and running, and it is three kilometres long. You can rent a small boat for twenty minutes for ten thousand soums. Children will love the large playground with swings, a climbing wall, and a water garden, which is open in summer only.

There is also a sports area with two football pitches, a basketball court, and a table tennis area. People can use them for free, but they must book a time on the park website at weekends.

For visitors who like quiet, there is a library garden with benches, where people can borrow books and read under the trees. There is also a small cafe, which sells tea, sandwiches, and ice cream. Dogs are welcome on the lawn, but they must stay on a lead.

The park will be open from six in the morning until ten at night. Parking is free for the first two hours, and there is a bicycle path from the town centre. Bus number eight stops at the main gate every ten minutes.

The opening day has a free concert at four o'clock, and the mayor will plant the last tree. Please bring your family and friends.

items.prompt: Why is there a power cut?
items.audio:
This is an important notice from the City Electricity Company. Tomorrow, Tuesday, there will be a planned power cut in the east of the city. We are sorry, but our workers must change some old cables, and it is not safe to work with electricity on.

The power will go off at nine in the morning and come back at three in the afternoon. This is six hours without electricity. The cut affects the Yangiobod district, the area around Green Hospital, and the streets near the football stadium. If you are not sure about your street, you can look at the map on our website or phone the helpline, which is open from seven in the morning.

How can you get ready? First, please charge your phones, laptops, and torches tonight. Second, if you work from home, save your files often and, if possible, work in a library or a cafe in another district. Third, keep your fridge and freezer doors closed, because food stays cold for several hours if you do not open them. Fourth, turn off your oven and your washing machine before nine, and do not turn them on again until the power returns, because a sudden return of electricity can break machines.

Green Hospital has its own generator, so it will work normally. Traffic lights near the stadium will not work, and police officers will help drivers at the main crossings. Please drive slowly there.

Water will not stop. However, the water pressure may be low on high floors, so fill a bottle or a bucket in the morning if you live on the ninth floor or above.

We will send a text message when the power returns. If it is still off at four, please call us. Thank you for your patience.

items.prompt: When does the festival begin?
items.audio:
Welcome to the Spring Music and Food Festival in Khiva. The festival begins this Friday and finishes on Sunday. Here is the timetable for the three days.

On Friday, the gates open at four in the afternoon. At five, there is the opening parade, with dancers in colourful costumes. It starts at the East Gate and ends in the main square. At seven, a famous singer, Shahzoda, will give a concert on the big stage. The first day finishes at ten with fireworks.

Saturday is the busiest day. From ten in the morning, children can join workshops, where they can make paper masks and clay pots. At noon, there is a cooking show, and the chef Rustam will show how to make plov for three hundred people. Everyone can taste it for free at one o'clock. In the afternoon, at three, a young band from Bukhara plays folk music. At six, there is a poetry evening in the old library, and tickets cost five thousand soums. Please book early, because there are only eighty seats.

On Sunday, the festival is quieter. At eleven, there is a bicycle tour around the old city walls, which takes ninety minutes. At two o'clock, a street theatre group will perform a funny story for families. The final concert starts at five and finishes at eight, when the festival closes.

Food stands are open on all three days from noon to nine. You can try sweet pastries, grilled fish, and fresh fruit juice. Please bring your own bottle, because water refills are free.

Tickets for the festival cost twenty thousand soums for one day, or fifty thousand for all three days. Children under ten enter free. Please arrive early, and wear comfortable shoes.

On Friday, the gates open at four in the afternoon. At five, there is the opening parade, with dancers in colourful costumes. It starts at the East Gate and ends in the main square. At seven, a famous singer, Shahzoda, will give a concert on the big stage. The first day finishes at ten with fireworks.

Saturday is the busiest day. From ten in the morning, children can join workshops, where they can make paper masks and clay pots. At noon, there is a cooking show, and the chef Rustam will show how to make plov for three hundred people. Everyone can taste it for free at one o'clock. In the afternoon, at three, a young band from Bukhara plays folk music. At six, there is a poetry evening in the old library, and tickets cost five thousand soums. Please book early, because there are only eighty seats.

On Sunday, the festival is quieter. At eleven, there is a bicycle tour around the old city walls, which takes ninety minutes. At two o'clock, a street theatre group will perform a funny story for families. The final concert starts at five and finishes at eight, when the festival closes.

Food stands are open on all three days from noon to nine. You can try sweet pastries, grilled fish, and fresh fruit juice. Please bring your own bottle, because water refills are free.

Tickets for the festival cost twenty thousand soums for one day, or fifty thousand for all three days. Children under ten enter free. Please arrive early, and wear comfortable shoes.

items.prompt: What did Aziza find on Monday morning?
items.audio:
On Monday morning, Aziza woke up and found water on the kitchen floor. The pipe under the sink was broken. She turned off the water, took her phone, and called a plumber named Mr Brown. A woman answered and said, Brown Plumbing, how can I help you? Aziza explained her problem. The woman asked for her address, and Aziza said it was number twelve, Garden Street, flat four. The woman asked if it was an emergency. Aziza said yes, because the water was running very fast before she turned it off.

The woman said the plumber could come at ten thirty. Aziza was happy, but then she remembered that she had a meeting at ten. She asked if the plumber could come at eleven. The woman checked the list and said that eleven was fine. She also told Aziza the price. The visit cost thirty dollars, and the new pipe would be about twenty dollars more. Aziza said that was no problem.

Before ending the call, the woman gave her some advice. She told Aziza to put a bucket under the pipe and to dry the floor with old towels. She also said Aziza should not use the sink until the plumber arrived. Aziza thanked her and wrote down the plumber's name, which was Peter.

At five to eleven, Aziza heard the doorbell. Peter was a tall man with a blue bag full of tools. He looked at the pipe and smiled. He said it was an old pipe and it was easy to change. In forty minutes he finished the job. Aziza paid him fifty dollars and thanked him again. Then she made tea for both of them, and Peter told her to check the pipes every year.

items.prompt: Why did the teacher leave a message?
items.answer: She could not reach the parent
items.audio:
Hello, this is Mrs Karimova, the class teacher of Dilnoza's class. I am calling about the school trip next week. I am sorry to leave a message, but I could not reach you this afternoon. Please listen carefully, because there are some changes.

First, the trip is now on Thursday and not on Wednesday. The weather forecast says it will rain on Wednesday, so we moved it. The bus will leave from the school gate at eight fifteen in the morning. Please bring your child before eight o'clock, because we need time to count the children and check the list.

Second, we are going to the science museum in the city centre. The visit will take about four hours. The children will see a space show and make a small robot. Lunch is not included in the ticket, so please give Dilnoza a sandwich, an apple, and a bottle of water. She should not bring sweets or fizzy drinks.

Third, the ticket costs eight dollars. You can pay me on Monday or Tuesday, in the classroom, before lessons start. If you cannot pay, please tell me and we will find a solution. I also need you to sign the paper which I gave Dilnoza last Friday. Without it, she cannot go on the bus.

Finally, the children should wear comfortable shoes and a warm jacket. They will come back to school at about four in the afternoon, so you can collect them then.

If you have any questions, please call me back on my mobile phone after six in the evening. Thank you very much, and have a nice day. Goodbye.
options: She could not reach the parent

items.audio:
Jasur had an appointment with his doctor on Friday at nine thirty. On Thursday evening, he got a bad cold. His nose was red, his head hurt, and he felt very tired. He decided to call the clinic and cancel the visit, because he did not want to give his cold to other people.

The next morning, he called the clinic at eight o'clock. A friendly receptionist called Nigora answered. Jasur said, Good morning, I would like to cancel my appointment for today at nine thirty. Nigora asked for his full name and date of birth. Jasur told her, and she found him on the computer. She said, I am sorry you are ill. Do you want to make a new appointment?

Jasur said he did, but only for next week, because he planned to stay in bed for the weekend. Nigora looked at the calendar. She said the doctor was free on Monday at four, or on Tuesday at ten fifteen. Jasur chose Tuesday, because he works in the afternoon on Monday. She wrote his name in the book and said she would send him a message to remind him the day before.

Then Nigora gave him some advice. She told him to drink hot tea with lemon, eat soup, and sleep a lot. If he had a high temperature, he should call the clinic again and not wait. Jasur thanked her and said goodbye.

On Saturday he felt a little better, and on Tuesday he went to the clinic. The doctor said it was only a cold and told him to rest for three more days.

items.prompt: Where did Malika see the advert?
items.audio:
Malika is a student, and she needs a flat near her university. She saw an advert on the internet for a small flat on Park Road. The advert said, one bedroom, a kitchen, and a balcony, two hundred and fifty dollars a month. She called the number in the advert. A man named Mr Rashidov answered the phone.

Malika said, Hello, I am calling about the flat on Park Road. Is it still free? He said yes and asked her some questions. He wanted to know if she was a student, if she had pets, and if she smoked. Malika said she was a student, she had a cat, and she did not smoke. Mr Rashidov thought for a moment. He said that cats were fine, but she must keep the flat clean.

Malika then asked about the price. He said the rent was two hundred and fifty dollars, and water and internet were included, but she must pay for gas and electricity. She also asked how far the flat was from the university. He said it was ten minutes on foot, and there was a bus stop near the door.

They agreed to meet on Saturday at eleven o'clock in front of the building. Mr Rashidov said he would bring the keys and show her every room. He also asked her to bring her passport and a letter from the university.

After the call, Malika was very excited. She wrote the date in her notebook, and she told her mother the good news. Her mother said she should check the windows and the heating carefully before she signed anything.

items.prompt: What was Sardor doing when the phone rang?
items.audio:
It was nine o'clock in the evening, and Sardor was watching a football match with his brother. Suddenly his phone rang. The number was new to him, but he answered it. A woman said, Hello, Anvar, is that you? I am so happy to hear you! Sardor was surprised. He said, Sorry, I am not Anvar. My name is Sardor. The woman laughed and said, Oh no, I must have the wrong number. I am very sorry.

Sardor said it was no problem. But the woman sounded worried. She explained that she was trying to call her cousin Anvar, who lives in Samarkand. She wanted to tell him that her train would arrive on Sunday and not on Saturday. She had his number in an old notebook, and maybe it was wrong.

Sardor felt sorry for her. He asked what number she was calling. She read the numbers slowly, and Sardor listened. He noticed that the last two numbers were in the wrong order. He told her, Try seven, nine at the end, not nine, seven. The woman said thank you and promised to try again.

Five minutes later, the phone rang again. It was the same woman. She said, Sardor, it worked! Anvar answered, and he will meet me at the station. I want to say thank you very much. She told him her name was Gulnora, and she invited him for tea if he ever visited her city.

Sardor smiled and told his brother the story. His brother said it was the nicest wrong number he had ever heard of. Then they went back to the match.

A woman said, Hello, Anvar, is that you? I am so happy to hear you! Sardor was surprised. He said, Sorry, I am not Anvar. My name is Sardor. The woman laughed and said, Oh no, I must have the wrong number. I am very sorry.

Sardor said it was no problem. But the woman sounded worried. She explained that she was trying to call her cousin Anvar, who lives in Samarkand. She wanted to tell him that her train would arrive on Sunday and not on Saturday. She had his number in an old notebook, and maybe it was wrong.

Sardor felt sorry for her. He asked what number she was calling. She read the numbers slowly, and Sardor listened. He noticed that the last two numbers were in the wrong order. He told her, Try seven, nine at the end, not nine, seven. The woman said thank you and promised to try again.

Five minutes later, the phone rang again. It was the same woman. She said, Sardor, it worked! Anvar answered, and he will meet me at the station. I want to say thank you very much. She told him her name was Gulnora, and she invited him for tea if he ever visited her city.

Sardor smiled and told his brother the story. His brother said it was the nicest wrong number he had ever heard of. Then they went back to the match.

items.prompt: Where did Kamola lose her wallet?
items.audio:
Last Tuesday, Kamola lost her wallet on the bus. She noticed it only when she arrived at work and wanted to buy a coffee. She looked in her bag, in her coat, and in every pocket, but the wallet was gone. It was a small red wallet, and it had her bank card, some money, and a photo of her grandmother. She felt terrible.

She went back to the bus station at lunchtime and asked the driver. The driver said nobody had given him a wallet. Kamola left her phone number and went home with a heavy heart.

That evening, at seven o'clock, she received a text message from a number she did not know. It said, Hello, my name is Timur. I found a red wallet on bus number twenty-two. Is it yours? There is a photo of an old lady inside. Kamola read the message three times and her eyes filled with tears. She called him at once.

Timur was a young man who worked at a bakery. He said he found the wallet under a seat. He opened it to find the owner's name, and he saw the photo and a card. He did not take anything. He offered to bring it to her the next day, but Kamola said she would come to the bakery herself.

On Wednesday morning, she went to the bakery on Lenin Street. Timur gave her the wallet, and she checked everything. All the money was inside. She wanted to give him a reward, but he said no. So she bought ten warm loaves of bread and thanked him with a big smile.

items.prompt: When did the Evans family arrive?
items.audio:
Mr and Mrs Evans arrived at a small hotel in Bukhara late on Friday evening. They were tired after a long flight. In their room, Mrs Evans noticed that the air conditioner did not work, and it was very hot. She picked up the phone near the bed and pressed the number for reception.

A young man answered. He said, Good evening, reception, this is Bobur. How can I help you? Mrs Evans explained that the air conditioner in room number two hundred and five was not working. Bobur apologised and said he would send a technician in ten minutes. He asked if they needed anything else.

Mrs Evans said they were hungry, but the restaurant was already closed. Bobur said the kitchen could prepare two sandwiches and a pot of tea for them. It would take about twenty minutes, and he would send it to their room. Mrs Evans was very pleased.

Then she asked about breakfast. Bobur said breakfast was served from seven to ten o'clock on the ground floor, next to the garden. He also told her that the hotel offered a free city tour on Saturday morning at nine. The guide would meet the guests in the lobby, and the tour would last three hours.

Ten minutes later, a technician knocked on the door and fixed the machine in fifteen minutes. Soon a waiter brought the food. The Evans family ate their sandwiches on the small balcony, listened to the quiet city, and went to bed. They decided to tell their friends about this friendly hotel.

items.prompt: How long did Farhod have a toothache?
items.audio:
Farhod had a toothache for three days. At first he thought it would go away, but on Wednesday the pain became very strong. He could not eat his dinner, and he could not sleep. On Thursday morning he decided to call a dentist.

He found the number of a clinic called Smile Dental on the internet. He called at nine o'clock, and a receptionist named Lola answered. Farhod said, Hello, I have a very bad toothache. Can I see a dentist today? Lola said she was sorry to hear that. She checked the computer and said that the first free time was at two forty in the afternoon with Doctor Yusupova.

Farhod said that time was fine. Lola asked for his name, his age, and his phone number. She also asked if he was afraid of dentists. Farhod laughed and said, A little. Lola told him not to worry, because Doctor Yusupova was kind and gentle.

Then Lola explained some rules. He should arrive ten minutes before the appointment to fill in a form. He should not eat or drink anything hot before the visit, and he should clean his teeth carefully. She said a check would cost fifteen dollars, and a filling would be more.

At two thirty, Farhod arrived at the clinic. The doctor looked at his tooth and said he had a small hole. She made a filling in half an hour, and the pain went away. At the end she told him to eat less sugar and visit the clinic every six months.
